items.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016
items.q: Because he said Lunceford’s band was like a show band kind of two-beat band.

ctx.x: And went to the Basie band, and Snooky said, “I had to learn how to play all over.”

That’s right he told me that too. Because he said Lunceford’s band was like a show band kind of two-beat band. And Basie was in four swinging. And he said a few times, he said, “I’m not making this.” And the guys in Basie’s band said, “yes, Snooky, you’re doing okay.” Marshall Royal said, “yeah, you’re doing okay.” And Snooky said, “I’m not making it.” He said, “yeah, yeah, yeah, you are.” He told me that several times. And he’s the voice of that band. And I tell my students the thing with Snooky is the accent with

him is what got the dynamic of the band. The accents where he put the accents, that was the dynamic of the band, and everything else was softer. So the accents made it dance and swing and bounce. And to me, and I think I’m right about this, I’m not very dogmatic about very many things, but he was on the band with Lester Young. And early on he knew Lester Young, he knew Billie Holliday, he knew all those people. And the band went through Kansas City well who was listening to Lester Young? Charlie Parker. And so to…
